text:
without much choice

and almost without meaning to,

he was a young man

on a bus

crossing North Carolina

headed

somewhere

and it began to snow

and the bus stopped

at a café

in the hills and

the passengers

went in.

he sat at the counter

with the others,

ordered and was

brought his food,

which was particularly good

as was the coffee.

The waitress was not

like the women he

had known.

She wasn’t putting on airs,

a natural humor flowed

from her.

The cook said

crazy things.

The dishwasher,

in back,

laughed

with a laugh

clean

and pleasant.

the young man watched

the snow through the

windows.

He wanted to stay

in that café

forever.

A strange feeling

flooded him:

that everything

was

beautiful

there,

that everything would always remain

beautiful

there.

then the driver

told the passengers

it was time to leave.

the young man

thought, I’ll stay

here, I’ll stay here.

But

he got up and followed

the others to

the bus.

He found his seat

and watched the café

through the window.

the bus started,

rounded a curve,

and went down the road,

away from the hills.

the young man

looked

ahead.

The other passengers

talked about other things

read

or

tried

to sleep.

they had not noticed

the magic.

the young man

rested his head

against the seat,

closed his eyes,

pretended

to sleep.

Nothing remained

but to listen to the

sound

of the engine,

the sound of the

wheels

in the snow.

translation.title: Nirvana
translation.editorial_note:
Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. Lowercase openings, spare lineation, and stanza spacing are retained.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
